title: About
text: I’m Vamsi Gudipati. I spent nearly 16 years at Ansys, the engineering simulation company, most recently as a Lead R&D Verification Engineer. Before that I was a CAD design engineer. Now I am moving into machine learning for engineering simulation, and I write here about what I learn. Since February 2026 I have been doing this as an independent consultant.

title: About
text:
What I work on
At Ansys I tested and validated simulation software, from geometry tools to cloud and high-performance computing platforms, and built the test automation and CI/CD pipelines behind it. That taught me to treat quality as part of the design, not a step at the end.
My focus now is scientific machine learning for fluids, structures and multiphysics: physics-informed neural networks, neural operators, reduced-order and surrogate models, digital twins, and reinforcement learning for flow control. One result so far: a neural-network surrogate that predicts steady laminar flow fields in about 50 milliseconds, where a traditional solver takes hours.
I care most about honest evaluation. A model for physics can look good and still be wrong, through leaked data, a weak baseline or results that break the physics.
I also build my own tools for checking scientific ML code, and I work with AI coding assistants every day.
